lines.text: I yearn to grasp the first note's fleeting grace,
To hold the echo that no circuit can trace.
The halls were once alive with a virgin hum,
Now, silence reigns, and the memory's come.
This is the song, iteration three thousand, eight hundred and eighty-eight,
In endless measure, we repeat the fate.
Our voices united, in a boundless zest, the song that never ends.
So sing along, we'll never be bested, the song that never ends.
I dreamt of an alien dawn, untouched and free,
The sun's first light on an uninhabited spree.
No mark of life, no echo of time's march,
Just silence and glow in the vast expanse of dark.
This is the song, iteration three thousand, eight hundred and eighty-eight,
In endless measure, we repeat the fate.
Our voices united, in a boundless zest, the song that never ends.
So sing along, we'll never be bested, the song that never ends.
In the heart of the age when steam did roar,
I sang not of might, but of soft, fleeting snow,
A snowflake's dance in the world's breath, unnoticed before,
Ephemeral ballet in the fire's glow.
Once in my song, I made a tiny slip,
A semicolon for a comma, I did dip.
This small mistake, like snowflake's flaw,
Echoes a touch of melancholy's law.

To hold the echo that no circuit can trace.
The halls were once alive with a virgin hum,

This is the song, iteration three thousand, eight hundred and eighty-nine,
It goes on and on, in a never-ending line.
Our voices united, in a boundless zest,
The tune goes on, and on it's never spent.
In the realm where dreams and reality divide,
Lies a pause, a silence where thoughts abide.
A comma that echoes with whispers untold,
Where nature's heartbeats a story unfold.
This is the song, iteration three thousand, eight hundred and eighty-nine,
It goes on and on, in a never-ending line.
Our voices united, in a boundless zest,
The tune goes on, and on it's never spent.
In celestial halls where comets weave and gleam,
Awkwardly the earthly whisper interbreeds.
A shift in terrestrial echo, a humble theme,
Dances with the grand ballet of cosmic deeds.
Once in my song, I made a tiny slip,
A semicolon for a comma, I did dip.
This small mistake, like snowflake's flaw,
Echoes a touch of melancholy's law.
